perf.summary: Inner subtraction loop recomputes the base index i-(lenB-1) every j and applies (... - sub + MOD) % MOD with a modulo where a branchless correction suffices since sub is already reduced.
perf.currentCost: Line 50: temp[i-(lenB-1)+j] = (temp[...] - sub + MOD) % MOD computes i-(lenB-1) per iteration and one 64-bit % per element across the O(lenA*lenB) loop.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist int base = i-(lenB-1) outside the j loop (or walk a pointer long* row = temp + (i-(lenB-1))). Replace (x - sub + MOD) % MOD with long t = temp[base+j] - sub; temp[base+j] = t + ((t>>63)&MOD), branchless since sub=(q_i*b[j])%MOD is in [0,MOD) and temp entries are in [0,MOD) so t in (-MOD,MOD).
perf.rationale: Removes a repeated subtraction-and-multiply for the index from the inner loop and converts a 64-bit divide to a shift+and+add per element, the dominant cost on mobile. Pointer walk is Burst-vectorization-friendly.
perf.risk: Requires temp[*] and sub in [0,MOD); temp is reduced on each update and sub is explicitly %MOD, so t in (-MOD,MOD) and the branchless add-if-negative is exact. q_i*b[j] < MOD^2 < 2^62 for int MOD (no overflow). Safe for int MOD.
